name: Fix a PR the merge queue sent back
description: A merge queue batch failed CI and the queue split it in halves until one PR alone was red. The queue sends that PR back to its build: fix what broke CI on its branch, note it on the build, push. The new head rejoins the queue by itself and is retested. Never merges to main.
author: AmberX AXF

inputs.label: Branch of the PR that broke the batch
Its build (orchestrator id), if it has one

data.brief:
The merge queue tested PR #{{pr}} (branch {{branch}}, build {{build}}) on its own on the latest main in batch {{batch}} and CI failed: {{failing}}. Run: {{run}}. This is fix try {{attempt}}.
1. Read the failed jobs' logs (gh run view, or the GitHub API with the token from framework/cli/github-token.mjs). Decide whether this PR's change causes the failure.
2. git fetch origin; check out {{branch}}; merge origin/main into it (never rebase, never force push).
3. Fix the cause on the branch, keeping the PR's intent. Run the failing checks and the touched plugins' and apps' own tests locally (heavy ones through node framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs heavy -- <cmd>) until they pass.
4. If the failure is not this PR's doing (main is red, a flaky or infrastructure job), push nothing and say so plainly in the report: the queue keeps it out until a new commit, and Brett decides.
5. Green: git push origin HEAD:{{branch}}. The PR rejoins the merge queue by itself and is retested. Never push to main, never merge a PR.
6. If build {{build}} is set: node apps/console-web/plugins/*/orchestrator.mjs act note {{build}} "Merge queue sent #{{pr}} back (batch {{batch}}, try {{attempt}}): <cause>, <fix>".
Report the cause, the fix, the files and the tests run.
